title: api-gateway: tune streaming proxy buffers, routing rules, and payload limits for OpenAI-compatibility
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Several customer reports and internal canaries exposed increased tail latency and intermittent stream truncation when handling long-running streaming responses that include function/tool-calling events and structured JSON output. Root cause analysis pointed to two interacting issues: (1) the streaming proxy was using a fixed small buffer and backpressure window that dropped or coalesced events for large payloads, and (2) routing rules would send large, tool-heavy requests to general-purpose pools that are optimized for throughput but not long-lived streaming connections. This PR adjusts the gateway behaviour to improve streaming stability and maintain OpenAI-compatible semantics for function calls and structured outputs.
Changes (high level):
- Increase streaming proxy write/read buffer sizes and make buffer growth adaptive instead of fixed; tune chunk flush thresholds to reduce partial event coalescing that broke structured output parsing.
- Add routing policy: requests with function/tool-calling markers, or with estimated output length (via client metadata or long-input heuristic), are routed to long-lived streaming nodes (streaming-specialized pool) which keep larger socket buffers and extended idle timeouts.
- Enforce conservative payload/prompt size limits for the streaming proxy path (server-side limit 1.2MB for streaming proxies; fall back to non-streaming path with 413 if exceeded) to avoid pathological memory growth under extreme client behaviour.
- Improve OpenAI-compatibility: ensure streaming event framing preserves top-level "choices" and "delta" sequences, and include explicit "function_call" events when model signals the call. Adjust the proxy to not strip or merge CRLF boundaries that some clients rely on for event parsing.
- Add metrics and tracing hooks: streaming.event_coalesce_count, streaming.buffer_resize_count, gateway.routed_to_stream_pool, and a tag to track openai_compat=true requests.
- Rollout plan and feature flagging: feature gated under feature_flag.gateway.streaming_stability (default enabled for 10% of traffic for 48h, then ramp).
Commits summary:
- Commit 1: refactor(gateway): extract streaming-proxy buffer manager, add adaptive growth policy
- Commit 2: perf(gateway): increase default buffer and chunk flush thresholds; add unit tests
- Commit 3: routing(gateway): add long-lived-stream pool selection and routing policy
- Commit 4: api(openai-compat): preserve function_call events and streaming framing tests
- Commit 5: observability: add metrics/tracing and dashboard templates
- Commit 6: docs: update API surface notes and rate-limit behavior for streaming path
Files changed (high level):
- gateway/proxy/streaming_proxy.go
- gateway/routing/policy.go
- gateway/routing/stream_pool.go
- api/openai_compat/streaming_formatter.go
- telemetry/metrics/streaming_metrics.yaml
- docs/gateway/streaming.md
- helm/values.gateway.yaml
- tests/integration/streaming_openai_compat_test.go
Testing:
- Added unit tests for buffer growth and framing preservation.
- Integration tests added in tests/integration that simulate function-call streaming sessions and validate event ordering and no truncation.
- Ran canary against perf-canary with 10k synthetic streaming sessions: 98th percentile latency improved by ~12% and event-drop incidents reduced from 18/day to 0 on the canary cluster.
- CI: build & unit tests passed; flaky integ test retried once and passed in subsequent run.
Backwards compatibility & breaking changes:
- This change is opt-in via feature flag during rollout; default will be enabled gradually. We intentionally keep the payload limit conservative and return 413 for streaming path only; non-streaming endpoints are unaffected. Clients relying on previously undocumented proxy buffering behaviour may see different event chunking semantics (improved, not worse) — recommended to consume SSE/event-streams by parsing events rather than relying on fixed chunk sizes.
Rollback plan:
- Feature flag off to revert routing and buffer changes.
- Hotfix branch prepared for fast revert if unexpected regression observed.
Notes for reviewers:
- Please pay attention to stream framing tests and the OpenAI-compat examples in tests/integration.
- Routing policy has unit tests simulating mixed workloads; more load testing on dedicated capacity clusters is desirable before global rollout.
Related: Linear ENG-4210 (streaming stability), ENG-4235 (routing policy), SUP-1123 (customer incident).

discussion: Jonas: Can we make the buffer growth cap configurable per-tenant? Reply Maya: yes, added helm value and tenant override option; default cap conservatively set.

Priya: How does this interact with Dedicated reserved pools? Reply Maya: routing policy prefers stream-specialized nodes; for Dedicated we add a label that admins can opt-in to have stream nodes in the reserved pool.
Ethan: CI integ test flaked once. Maya: added a retry and extended test timeout; observed transient infra flakiness unrelated to logic.
release_notes: Gateway: Improved streaming stability and OpenAI-compatible function-calling semantics. Increased streaming proxy buffer adaptively, added routing to long-lived streaming pool for function/tool-calling workloads, and enforced conservative streaming-path payload limits (413 when exceeded). Added metrics and tracing to monitor streaming coalescing and buffer growth.
